<description>
**Problem:** The orphanage can abort when more than 3,000 peers have orphan announcements.
The `-maxconnections` setting currently has no explicit upper bound.

**Fix:** Cap `-maxconnections` at 2,000 with a warning before reserving file descriptors, while retaining the default of 200.
</description>

<commits>
ec01169832 p2p: cap maxconnections at 2000

Limit the configurable automatic peer count to 2000, leaving headroom
below the default orphanage latency limit.

Apply the cap before reserving file descriptors. Use saturating `int`
parsing so oversized arguments cannot wrap before the cap is applied.
</commits>

<previous_description>
{
 "summary": "Prevents an assertion abort in the transaction orphanage when more than 3,000 peers have active orphan announcements. Floors the per-peer latency allowance at one during trimming calculations and allows peers with a DoS score of exactly one to be selected for eviction. Updates documentation, unit tests, and fuzz coverage to reflect the floored share.",
 "problem": "The orphanage calculates a peer's latency limit by dividing a global score (default 3,000) by the number of peers currently holding orphans. When more than 3,000 peers announce orphans, integer division evaluates the per-peer limit to zero, causing an assertion failure in GetDosScore() during trimming and crashing the node. This affects nodes configured with unusually high connection limits on operating systems supporting high file descriptor counts.",
 "card": "Prevents a node abort in the transaction orphanage when high peer counts exceed the default global latency limit of 3,000. When more than 3,000 peers announce orphans, integer division sets each peer's latency allowance to zero, causing an assertion crash when GetDosScore() calculates peer eviction priority. The fix floors the peer latency allowance at one during trimming and permits eviction of peers with a DoS score of exactly one. This crash only affects nodes configured with connection limits well above the default of 200.",
